trickyParts: #2449 removed Dispatch's SSE endpoint and loadgen's SSE client; the commit this issue measures serves only SSE, so loadgen probes /ws/live once per step and falls back to /api/v1/events on a 404 handshake.

browsertype typed into the 'Revision token rN' paragraph that loadgen's edits replace, failing every later edit and upload of a typed document; cluster.sh passes -protect 'Revision token' and up refuses a driver without it, before the lock.
The 5 s sampler's text heap read took 29% of Dispatch's CPU in the replay; it now reads the binary profile off its loop. Results v4 carries only fixed-sampler runs.

The heartbeat renews the lock only while a registered command of the run is the same live process (pid and /proc start time in <run>/commands/); a script's gap between two commands can stop it, and the next command's ensure_daemons starts it again.
Main's reference seed (#2469) runs in both stack.sh and cluster.sh seed; its request_keys delete moved into loadgen seed-finish, which both share.
deviations: The reference-seed rerun of the full curves and the hour (results v5) runs after INFRA-707's passes, as the architect decided; this round's 100Gi default rests on a 20-minute typed replay's 9.4 GiB peak, and each step of that rerun records its pg-disk.json peak.
A typed replay still loses edits where typing changed the logged text (68 named and 44 unnamed edits in the 20-minute r16-typing); the README says typed replays are not compared with the outage.
The tester's cases (o) and (p) keep their shellcheck notes; CI runs no shellcheck on cluster.test.sh.

The four cluster files are exceptions under 'a CI job runs it, and it fetches nothing' rather than the architect's suggested 'no CI job runs it' for three of them: envoy-go runs cluster.test.sh, which sources cluster.sh, templates nats.yaml and runs render-nats.sh --pin-from, so 'no CI job runs it' would be false; none of them hands an image to a registry in CI.
